subject: Chemistry
title: Introduction to Chemistry: Branches and Careers
summary: A guided introduction to what chemistry studies, the major branches of the field, and the work people do with chemistry.
focus: Match organic, inorganic, physical, analytical, and biochemistry to what each one investigates.
Connect chemistry to real work in health, industry, food, the environment, and research.
Use the examples in the notes to explain why chemistry is part of everyday life.

subject: Chemistry
title: Laboratory Skills, Safety, and Separation Methods
summary: Practice the careful laboratory habits behind measuring, heating, handling materials, and separating mixtures.
focus: Name the equipment used to measure mass and handle small amounts of solids.
Choose filtration, decantation, evaporation, or another method from the properties of a mixture.
Review safe heating and reagent-handling habits before a practical activity.

subject: Chemistry
title: Atomic Theory: Evidence, Models, and Dalton’s Postulates
summary: Trace how observations and experiments led to the idea that matter is made of atoms, then review Dalton’s atomic theory.
focus: State the major ideas in Dalton’s theory in your own words.
Explain how evidence such as microscopy supports atomic models.
Separate the historical model from ideas later refined by modern chemistry.

subject: Chemistry
title: Atomic Models and Quantum Mechanical Theory
summary: Compare the Bohr model with the modern quantum model and use quantum numbers to describe electrons and orbitals.
focus: Compare fixed Bohr energy levels with the probability-based quantum model.
Know what the principal, angular momentum, magnetic, and spin quantum numbers describe.
Relate orbitals, sublevels, and electron location to atomic structure.

subject: Chemistry
title: Developing and Reading the Periodic Table
summary: Follow the historical organization of elements and learn how groups, periods, families, and blocks make the periodic table useful.
focus: Recognize early classification ideas such as Döbereiner’s triads.
Locate periods, groups, transition metals, lanthanides, and actinides.
Use an element’s position to predict broad similarities with other elements.

subject: Chemistry
title: Atomic Number, Mass Number, and Isotopes
summary: Use atomic notation to count subatomic particles and distinguish mass number from average atomic mass.
focus: Find protons, neutrons, and electrons from atomic number and mass number.
Write and interpret standard isotope notation.
Explain isotopes and calculate or interpret weighted average atomic mass.

subject: Chemistry
title: Molecular Geometry and Polarity
summary: Use electron domains, bond angles, and lone pairs to explain molecular shape and overall polarity.
focus: Apply VSEPR to identify common molecular shapes.
Show how lone pairs change geometry and bond angles.
Decide whether bond dipoles cancel or create a polar molecule.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nomenclature of Acids
summary: Learn the naming patterns for binary acids and oxyacids, including the link between anion endings and acid names.
focus: Distinguish binary acids from oxyacids using their formulas.
Convert -ide, -ate, and -ite endings into the correct acid names.
Recognize mono-, di-, and triprotic acids from the number of ionizable hydrogens.

subject: Chemistry
title: Chemical Bonding and VSEPR Geometry
summary: Connect electron sharing and lone pairs to Lewis structures, molecular shapes, and the behavior of covalent substances.
focus: Read or draw Lewis structures before deciding on a shape.
Count bonding pairs and lone pairs around the central atom.
Compare related VSEPR shapes and explain the effect of lone pairs.

subject: EffCom
title: Visual Data, Evidence, and Objective Communication
summary: Read visual information closely and communicate findings with evidence instead of unsupported assumptions.
focus: Read titles, labels, scales, and categories before interpreting a chart or infographic.
Separate a direct observation from an inference or personal claim.
Use accurate, objective wording when explaining data.

subject: EffCom
title: Visual Representations and Non-Linear Text
summary: Transform linear information into charts, diagrams, and other visual forms that make relationships and key ideas easier to see.
focus: Explain when a visual representation communicates better than a long paragraph.
Identify trends, comparisons, relationships, and key ideas in a visual.
Turn a short sequence of information into an appropriate non-linear form.

subject: EffCom
title: Summarizing and Paraphrasing Technical Writing
summary: Practice shortening technical material without losing its meaning and restating ideas without copying the original wording.
focus: Identify the central idea and the essential supporting details.
Distinguish a summary from a paraphrase.
Keep the original meaning while using your own structure and language.

subject: EffCom
title: Academic Communication: Term 2 Foundations
summary: A term-opening Effective Communication resource for building clear, purposeful academic communication and group work habits.
focus: Use the opening activities to identify the communication skill being practiced.
Keep audience, purpose, and clarity in mind when responding to tasks.
Track group responsibilities and turn the source pages into your own study notes.

subject: GenMath
title: Bearing and Navigation: Applied Triangle Problems
summary: Use bearings with the sine rule, cosine rule, and triangle diagrams to solve navigation situations.
focus: Draw north lines and label bearings correctly.
Choose the sine rule or cosine rule from the information given.
Check whether the final direction is written as a bearing, not just an angle.

subject: GenMath
title: Introduction to Trigonometric Ratios
summary: Build the right-triangle meaning of sine, cosine, and tangent before using them in calculations.
focus: Label opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse relative to the chosen angle.
Choose sine, cosine, or tangent from the two sides involved.
Use calculator mode and rounding appropriately.

subject: GenMath
title: Applications of Trigonometry: More Problems
summary: Apply trigonometric ratios to contextual problems by translating words into a diagram and a solvable equation.
focus: Sketch the situation before selecting a trig ratio.
Identify the requested measurement and the known sides or angles.
Give a final answer with sensible units and precision.

subject: GenMath
title: Piecewise Function Applications
summary: Use piecewise rules to model situations whose formula changes across different input ranges.
focus: Match each interval with the correct rule.
Evaluate a piecewise function at boundary values carefully.
Interpret the function in the real situation it represents.

subject: GenMath
title: Standard Deviation and Data Spread
summary: Measure how far data values typically sit from the mean and compare the consistency of data sets.
focus: Find or verify the mean before measuring deviations.
Interpret a smaller or larger standard deviation in context.
Avoid confusing the center of data with its spread.

subject: GenMath
title: Types of Data and Measurement Scales
summary: Classify data and recognize the measurement scale that determines which comparisons and calculations make sense.
focus: Distinguish qualitative from quantitative data.
Identify nominal, ordinal, interval, and ratio scales.
Choose examples that justify the scale, not just the topic.

subject: GenMath
title: Data Management and Statistics as a Tool
summary: See how mathematics is used to organize, interpret, and communicate information from real situations.
focus: Identify the question a data set is meant to answer.
Select a useful representation for the type of data.
Explain a conclusion without overstating what the data proves.

subject: GenMath
title: Term 2 Mathematics: Week 1 Foundations
summary: A Week 1 resource that sets up the concepts and problem-solving routines used in the term’s mathematics work.
focus: Follow definitions, examples, and worked solutions in order.
Write down unfamiliar notation with its meaning.
Use the source material as a reference while building your own examples.

subject: GenMath
title: Sine and Cosine Rules for Oblique Triangles
summary: Solve triangles without a right angle by deciding whether the sine rule or cosine rule fits the known information.
focus: Recognize SSS, SAS, ASA, and SSA information patterns.
Pair each angle with its opposite side in the sine rule.
Use the cosine rule correctly when two sides and an included angle are known.

subject: GenMath
title: Sine Rule and Area of Oblique Triangles
summary: Use the sine rule and included-angle area formula to solve non-right triangle problems.
focus: Keep opposite side-angle pairs aligned.
Check the possible ambiguous case when using the sine rule.
Use one-half ab sine C for the area of an oblique triangle.

subject: GenMath
title: Solving Right and Oblique Triangle Problems
summary: Choose a reliable strategy for triangle problems and verify that the completed triangle is reasonable.
focus: Decide first whether the triangle is right or oblique.
Choose a trigonometric ratio, sine rule, or cosine rule deliberately.
Check that side and angle sizes agree with the diagram.

subject: GenMath
title: Practice: Right and Oblique Triangle Problems
summary: A companion practice set for applying the appropriate triangle-solving method without skipping the diagram and checking stages.
focus: Organize given information before calculating.
Show the formula substitution instead of only the calculator result.
Compare your answer with the visual size of the triangle.

subject: GenMath
title: Angles of Elevation and Depression
summary: Model line-of-sight situations with right triangles, horizontal reference lines, and trigonometric ratios.
focus: Draw the horizontal line before marking elevation or depression angles.
Use the complementary angle only when the diagram requires it.
State the final height or distance with units.

subject: GenMath
title: Bearings and Navigation: Concepts and Conversions
summary: Learn the notation and diagram conventions needed before solving bearing and navigation questions.
focus: Measure bearings clockwise from north.
Write bearings as three-digit angles where required.
Translate a direction phrase into a labelled sketch.

subject: GenMath
title: Bearings and Navigation: Guided Practice
summary: Use navigation diagrams and bearings in structured practice problems.
focus: Mark north at every location when a route changes direction.
Separate interior triangle angles from compass bearings.
Use the correct triangle rule after the route diagram is complete.

subject: GenMath
title: Bearings and Navigation: Day 2 Practice
summary: Continue applying bearing notation and triangle methods to multi-step travel and location problems.
focus: Keep a consistent scale or clear labels in route sketches.
Track each leg of a journey separately.
Give both distance and direction when the question asks for a location.

subject: GenMath
title: Perimeter: Everyday Measurement Problems
summary: Use perimeter formulas and careful unit conversion to solve practical measurement questions.
focus: Identify which boundary lengths belong in the perimeter.
Convert units before adding measurements.
Explain what the total perimeter means in the situation.

subject: GenSci
title: Household Chemicals: Uses, Risks, and Safe Handling
summary: Identify familiar chemical substances, connect their formulas to everyday uses, and consider their health and safety risks.
focus: Match a household substance with its common use.
Read formulas and names accurately.
Describe safe handling or storage choices based on the substance’s risk.

subject: GenSci
title: Mixtures and Methods of Separation
summary: Separate mixtures by using differences in particle size, solubility, density, boiling point, or magnetism.
focus: Choose a separation method from the properties of the components.
Plan the order of steps for a salt, sand, and water mixture.
Explain what remains and what passes through at each step.

subject: GenSci
title: Osmosis, Tonicity, and Cell Water Balance
summary: Explain water movement across cell membranes and predict what happens to cells in hypotonic, isotonic, and hypertonic solutions.
focus: State the direction water moves during osmosis.
Compare hypertonic, hypotonic, and isotonic environments.
Relate water movement to cell swelling, shrinking, or balance.

subject: GenSci
title: Body Systems and Interdependence
summary: Explore how body systems work together and how an injury or change in one system can affect the rest of the body.
focus: Identify the systems involved in the situations from the notes.
Explain one chain of effects from injury to body function.
Connect prevention and healthy choices to system performance.

subject: GenSci
title: Respiratory Gas Exchange and Diffusion
summary: Study how oxygen and carbon dioxide move between alveoli and blood through diffusion.
focus: Locate the alveoli and nearby capillaries in a diagram.
Explain diffusion using concentration differences.
Relate thin surfaces, moisture, and surface area to efficient gas exchange.

subject: GenSci
title: Nervous System: Organization and Control
summary: Organize the nervous system into central and peripheral divisions and trace sensory and motor pathways.
focus: Differentiate the CNS from the PNS.
Compare sensory and motor divisions.
Separate somatic and autonomic responses using examples.

subject: GenSci
title: The Brain and Its Major Regions
summary: Identify major brain structures and connect each region to the functions it helps control.
focus: Locate the cerebrum, cerebellum, and brain stem.
Match a major region with its core function.
Use a scenario to infer which brain area may be involved.

subject: LCS
title: Career Planning: Factors and Personal Fit
summary: Plan career options by considering interests, values, skills, education, work culture, labour demand, and financial goals.
focus: Separate personal interests and values from outside job-market factors.
Identify evidence that a career path fits your strengths.
Compare career choices without treating salary as the only factor.

subject: LCS
title: Career Mapping: Skills, Interests, and Pathways
summary: Map personal strengths and interests to possible careers, then identify the training and qualifications each path needs.
focus: List skills, interests, and talents with specific examples.
Connect a possible career to its required education or training.
Use a career map to identify a next realistic step.

subject: LCS
title: Culture, Values, and Career Choices
summary: Examine how culture, family, community expectations, social prestige, and diversity can shape career decisions.
focus: Recognize cultural and social influences without stereotyping people.
Compare individual priorities with collective or family expectations.
Explain how gender and diversity considerations can affect opportunity.

subject: LCS
title: Researching Careers and Opportunities
summary: Use reliable channels such as online platforms, career fairs, and professional networks to research work opportunities.
focus: Compare the strengths of different career-information sources.
Check a source for credibility and current information.
Record skills, qualifications, and opportunities that repeat across sources.

subject: LCS
title: Compensation, Benefits, and Rewards
summary: Understand how base pay, benefits, incentives, and recognition form an employee’s total compensation.
focus: Distinguish wages or salary from non-cash benefits.
Explain how merit pay and incentives work.
Compare offers by looking at the full compensation package.

subject: LCS
title: Employee Rights and Workplace Protections
summary: Learn why clear rights, protections, and fair workplace practices matter for employees and organizations.
focus: Identify the purpose of employee rights in a workplace.
Recognize the difference between a policy and a basic protection.
Use respectful steps for raising a workplace concern.

subject: LCS
title: Leave, Breaks, and Worker Well-Being
summary: Evaluate how leave and break policies support health, fairness, productivity, and sustainable work.
focus: Explain why breaks and leave matter beyond convenience.
Compare policy choices from both employee and employer perspectives.
Relate reasonable work patterns to well-being and performance.

subject: LCS
title: Workplace Rules, Ethics, and Company Guidelines
summary: Use workplace rules and ethical thinking to create a safe, fair, and accountable organization.
focus: Distinguish legal compliance from ethical responsibility.
Explain why safety and fairness need clear guidelines.
Apply a guideline to a realistic workplace situation.

subject: LCS
title: Creating Company Guidelines
summary: Design practical company guidelines that are aligned, feasible, original, and ready to communicate to a team.
focus: Write a guideline with a clear purpose and audience.
Check whether the rule can realistically be followed.
Use the rubric to improve clarity, relevance, and completeness.

subject: LCS
title: Workplace Safety Training and Hazard Communication
summary: Learn the parts of effective safety training, including orientations, refreshers, hazards, and communication systems.
focus: Recognize common hazard symbols and what they communicate.
Explain why training must continue after an initial orientation.
Describe how workers should receive and act on safety information.

subject: LCS
title: Employment Compliance and Workforce Rules
summary: Review workplace compliance issues involving job classifications, probation, evaluation, and responsible management.
focus: Recognize why employment rules apply regardless of job title.
Explain the purpose of a fair probation or evaluation process.
Identify risks when workers are misclassified or managed inconsistently.

subject: LCS
title: Work-Life Balance and Healthy Workplaces
summary: Study work-life balance as a workplace practice that supports health, focus, and long-term performance.
focus: Identify signs that work demands are becoming unsustainable.
Suggest practical habits or policies that support balance.
Explain why healthy workplaces benefit both workers and organizations.

subject: LCS
title: Workplace Improvement and Employee Engagement
summary: Improve workplace culture through open communication, trust, inclusion, recognition, and useful feedback.
focus: Describe how feedback can improve a team when it is specific and respectful.
Connect inclusion and trust to employee engagement.
Choose an improvement strategy that fits the problem described.

subject: LCS
title: Professionalism and Workplace Etiquette
summary: Practice the respectful, responsible, and clear behavior expected in professional settings.
focus: Use respectful communication in both formal and everyday work situations.
Recognize accountability and reliability as professional habits.
Explain how etiquette affects teamwork and trust.

subject: LCS
title: Professional Respect and Digital Netiquette
summary: Apply professional respect to online messages, digital spaces, and workplace communication.
focus: Write messages with an appropriate tone and purpose.
Recognize how online choices can affect professional relationships.
Use netiquette to prevent misunderstandings and maintain respect.

subject: MabKom
title: Multimodal Academic and Technical Communication
summary: Use language, visuals, tone, and structure appropriately when communicating academic and technical ideas to an audience.
focus: Adjust tone and language to the audience and purpose.
Explain how visuals and words work together in a multimodal text.
Use context clues and strategies for unfamiliar vocabulary.

subject: MabKom
title: Project Proposal: Pagtugon sa Pangangailangan ng Kurso
summary: Plan and communicate a project proposal that responds to a course need with clear goals, details, and documentation.
focus: Identify the need the proposal should answer.
Organize a proposal into a logical and persuasive sequence.
Use meeting notes, plans, and supporting details responsibly.

subject: MabKom
title: Mabisang Komunikasyon: Second-Term Course Guide
summary: Use the second-term plan as a map of the course topics, tasks, and communication skills to develop.
focus: Track the order of lessons and major requirements.
Connect planned activities to the communication skill they build.
Turn the course guide into a personal study schedule.

subject: PKLP
subjectLabel: Pag-aaral ng Kasaysayan at Lipunang Pilipino
title: PKLP: Term 2 Note Collection
summary: A source collection for the Term 2 Pag-aaral ng Kasaysayan at Lipunang Pilipino lessons. Read the pages in sequence and build a timeline as you review.
focus: Identify the people, places, dates, and terms that recur across the notes.
Connect events to their causes, effects, and historical context.
Use the original pages to verify names, sequences, and source-based claims.
